text: In 1902, a city started paying people for rat tails. Just the tails.
Hanoi, French colonial Vietnam. The French built shiny new sewers under their quarter.
Rats loved them. They climbed out of toilets, and plague was spreading across Asia.
So the city made an offer: reportedly one cent for every rat tail.
It worked. At the peak, over twenty thousand tails came in a single day.
Then officials spotted something odd: rats running around with no tails.
People cut off the tail, let the rat go, and let it breed more tails.
Inspectors even found rat farms outside the city.
The hunt failed, and the plague came anyway.
Not hunters. Money. Pay for tails, and you get tails, not fewer rats.
